title: The secondary mountain and the transport of regular anchors

blocks.tex:
This chapter supplies the two layers of the production step of
\cref{thm:four_active_adjacent_unequal} which sit between the original word
and the three native producers of \cref{chap:discrete_native_first_pair}
and \cref{chap:discrete_native_repeated_negative}.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{The secondary mountain}
    (\cref{sec:mt_peak} and \cref{sec:mt_mountain}).  In an adjacent-unequal DFV word
    with a marked maximum $H$, choose a strict local maximum $q\ne H$ of
    largest value.  If $\kappa_q<\kappa_H$, the readings strictly above
    $\kappa_q$ form one ordinary interval of offsets from $q$, strictly
    rising to $H$ and strictly falling after it
    (\cref{thm:mt_mountain}).  This is proved by finite induction along
    actual consecutive indices of the original cyclic word; nothing is
    pruned or compressed, and there is no bound on $n$ or on the number of
    distinct readings.
  \item \textbf{Transport of anchors}
    (\cref{sec:mt_scale}, \cref{sec:mt_slots}, \cref{sec:mt_frames} and \cref{sec:mt_normalize}).
    Regular four-edge anchors (\cref{def:regular_four_anchor}) are carried
    along positive rescaling, the cyclic shift $i\mapsto i+1$ and the
    reflection $i\mapsto-i$ of the word.  The anchor itself is
    transported --- frame, half-lengths, zero and surjective derivative
    --- not merely the realization property.  The rescaling and the two
    slot permutations are exact identities of controllers off their zero
    set, which are then differentiated at the zero; the cyclic identity
    keeps a lifted-turn correction whose derivative survives.
\end{enumerate}
\Cref{sec:mt_normalize} assembles these into the normalization at the
selected peak and the two terminal-flag branches used by
\cref{thm:four_active_adjacent_unequal}.

Throughout, $n\ne0$ where cyclic indices are used, $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$,
and for $x\in\ZMod n$ we write $\operatorname{val}(x)\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$
for its natural representative.  A natural number $m$ acts on $\ZMod n$
through its cast, so $i+m$ is the $m$-th successor of $i$.

blocks.title: The highest secondary peak and its high paths

blocks.tex:
The selected peak is \cref{def:four_active_secondary_peak}: $q\ne H$ is a
strict local maximum (\cref{def:zz_local_max}), and $\kappa_i\le\kappa_q$
for every strict local maximum $i\ne H$.  Neither positivity nor any
distinctness of nonadjacent readings enters the combinatorial lemmas of this
and the next section; only the adjacent inequality
$\kappa_i\ne\kappa_{i+1}$ is used.  A reading is \emph{high} if it is
strictly larger than $\kappa_q$.

blocks.label: lem:mt_secondary_exists
blocks.title: existence of the highest secondary peak
blocks.body:
Let $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$ hold and $\kappa_i\ne\kappa_{i+1}$ for
  every $i$.  For every $H\in\ZMod n$ there is a highest secondary peak $q$
  for $H$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_highestSecondaryPeak
lean.code:
theorem exists_highestSecondaryPeak {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) (H : ZMod n) :
    ∃ q, HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij, hi, hj⟩ := hdfv.exists_two_strictLocalMax hne
  let s := Finset.univ.filter (fun i : ZMod n => i ≠ H ∧ IsStrictLocalMax κ i)
  have hs : s.Nonempty := by
    by_cases hiH : i = H
    · exact ⟨j, by simp [s, hj, show j ≠ H by intro e; exact hij (hiH.trans e.symm)]⟩
    · exact ⟨i, by simp [s, hiH, hi]⟩
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hmax⟩ := s.exists_max_image κ hs
  have hqm : q ≠ H ∧ IsStrictLocalMax κ q := by simpa [s] using hq
  exact ⟨q, hqm.1, hqm.2, fun i hiH hi => hmax i (by simp [s, hiH, hi])⟩

deps.title: a window gives two distinct strict local maxima
deps.label: thm:n6mr_two_strict_max

blocks.tex:
By \cref{thm:n6mr_two_strict_max} there are two distinct indices $i\ne j$,
  both strict local maxima of $\kappa$.  At least one of them differs from
  $H$: if $i=H$ then $j\ne H$.  Hence the finite set
  $S=\{i\in\ZMod n: i\ne H,\ i\text{ a strict local maximum}\}$ is nonempty,
  and $\kappa$ attains a maximum on $S$ at some $q$.  By construction
  $q\ne H$, $q$ is a strict local maximum, and $\kappa_i\le\kappa_q$ for all
  $i\in S$, which is the maximality clause.  Only the existence of two
  strict maxima is used; there may be many more, and the argument does not
  use any conclusion specific to $n=6$ from the chapter of
  \cref{thm:n6mr_two_strict_max}.

blocks.label: lem:mt_high_step
blocks.title: one step of a high path
blocks.body:
Let $q$ be a highest secondary peak for $H$, and let $i\ne H$ be high,
  $\kappa_q<\kappa_i$.  Then $i$ is not a strict local maximum.  If
  moreover the word is adjacent-unequal, then
  \[
    \kappa_{i-1}<\kappa_i\ \Longrightarrow\ \kappa_i<\kappa_{i+1},
    \qquad
    \kappa_{i+1}<\kappa_i\ \Longrightarrow\ \kappa_i<\kappa_{i-1}.
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.backward_step
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.backward_step {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1)) (hi : i ≠ H)
    (hhigh : κ q < κ i) (hrise : κ (i + 1) < κ i) :
    κ i < κ (i - 1) := by
  by_contra h
  have hprev : κ (i - 1) ≠ κ i := by simpa using hne (i - 1)
  have hfall : κ (i - 1) < κ i := lt_of_le_of_ne (le_of_not_gt h) hprev
  exact hq.not_isStrictLocalMax hi hhigh ⟨hfall, hrise⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.not_isStrictLocalMax
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.not_isStrictLocalMax {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hi : i ≠ H) (hhigh : κ q < κ i) : ¬ IsStrictLocalMax κ i := by
  intro hpeak
  exact (not_le_of_gt hhigh) (hq.maximal i hi hpeak)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.forward_step
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.forward_step {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1)) (hi : i ≠ H)
    (hhigh : κ q < κ i) (hrise : κ (i - 1) < κ i) :
    κ i < κ (i + 1) := by
  by_contra h
  have hfall : κ (i + 1) < κ i := lt_of_le_of_ne (le_of_not_gt h) (hne i).symm
  exact hq.not_isStrictLocalMax hi hhigh ⟨hrise, hfall⟩

blocks.tex:
If $i$ were a strict local maximum, maximality of $q$ would give
  $\kappa_i\le\kappa_q<\kappa_i$.  For the forward implication suppose
  $\kappa_{i-1}<\kappa_i$ but not $\kappa_i<\kappa_{i+1}$.  Since
  $\kappa_{i+1}\ne\kappa_i$, we get $\kappa_{i+1}<\kappa_i$, and then $i$ is a
  strict local maximum, which was excluded.  The backward implication is
  symmetric, using $\kappa_{i-1}\ne\kappa_i$ (adjacent inequality at $i-1$).

A strict rise into a high reading away from $H$ therefore continues in the
same direction.  The next two lemmas iterate this along actual consecutive
indices and stop exactly at $H$.

blocks.label: lem:mt_cyclic_distance
blocks.title: cyclic distances
blocks.body:
For $i,H\in\ZMod n$ put $d=\operatorname{val}(H-i)<n$ and
  $d'=\operatorname{val}(i-H)<n$.  Then $i+d=H$ and $i-d'=H$, and
  $i+m\ne H$ for every natural $m<d$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.cyclic_offset_ne_of_lt_distance
lean.code:
theorem cyclic_offset_ne_of_lt_distance {i H : ZMod n} {m : ℕ}
    (hm : m < (H - i).val) : i + (m : ZMod n) ≠ H := by
  intro h
  have hcast : (m : ZMod n) = H - i := by
    exact eq_sub_iff_add_eq.mpr (by simpa [add_comm] using h)
  have hv := congrArg ZMod.val hcast
  rw [ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt (lt_trans hm (ZMod.val_lt _))] at hv
  omega

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.cyclic_distance_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem cyclic_distance_endpoints (i H : ZMod n) :
    i + ((H - i).val : ZMod n) = H ∧ i - ((i - H).val : ZMod n) = H := by
  simp only [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
  constructor <;> ring

blocks.tex:
The cast of $\operatorname{val}(x)$ is $x$, so $i+d=i+(H-i)=H$ and
  $i-d'=i-(i-H)=H$.  If $i+m=H$ with $m<d$, then $m=H-i$ in $\ZMod n$; since
  $m<d<n$, taking natural representatives gives $m=\operatorname{val}(H-i)=d$,
  a contradiction.

blocks.label: lem:mt_cyclic_path
blocks.title: monotone cyclic paths
blocks.body:
Let $\lambda\in\RR$, $i,H\in\ZMod n$, $d=\operatorname{val}(H-i)$, and
  assume the propagation rule: for every $j\ne H$ with $\lambda<\kappa_j$
  and $\kappa_{j-1}<\kappa_j$ one has $\kappa_j<\kappa_{j+1}$.  If
  $\lambda<\kappa_i$ and either
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $\kappa_{i-1}<\kappa_i$ (an incoming rise), or
    \item $\kappa_i<\kappa_{i+1}$ (an outgoing first rise),
  \end{enumerate}
  then $\lambda<\kappa_{i+m}$ for every $m\le d$, and $m\mapsto\kappa_{i+m}$
  is strictly increasing on $\{0,\dots,d\}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_rising
lean.code:
theorem strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_rising {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {level : ℝ} {i H : ZMod n}
    (hstep : ∀ j, j ≠ H → level < κ j → κ (j - 1) < κ j → κ j < κ (j + 1))
    (hhigh : level < κ i) (hrise : κ (i - 1) < κ i) :
    (∀ m ≤ (H - i).val, level < κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (H - i).val) := by
  have hchain : ∀ m, m ≤ (H - i).val →
      level < κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) ∧
      κ (i + (m : ZMod n) - 1) < κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero => intro _; simpa using And.intro hhigh hrise
    | succ m ih =>
      intro hm
      have hm' : m < (H - i).val := by omega
      obtain ⟨hhighm, hrisem⟩ := ih (by omega)
      have hnext := hstep (i + (m : ZMod n))
        (cyclic_offset_ne_of_lt_distance hm') hhighm hrisem
      constructor
      · simpa [Nat.cast_add, add_assoc] using lt_trans hhighm hnext
      · simpa [Nat.cast_add, ← add_assoc] using hnext
  refine ⟨fun m hm => (hchain m hm).1, ?_⟩
  apply strictMonoOn_Iic_of_lt_succ
  intro m hm
  have hnext := hstep (i + (m : ZMod n))
    (cyclic_offset_ne_of_lt_distance hm) (hchain m hm.le).1 (hchain m hm.le).2
  simpa [Nat.cast_add, add_assoc] using hnext

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_first_step
lean.code:
theorem strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_first_step {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {level : ℝ} {i H : ZMod n}
    (hstep : ∀ j, j ≠ H → level < κ j → κ (j - 1) < κ j → κ j < κ (j + 1))
    (hhigh : level < κ i) (hrise : κ i < κ (i + 1)) :
    (∀ m ≤ (H - i).val, level < κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (H - i).val) := by
  have hchain : ∀ m, m ≤ (H - i).val →
      level < κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) ∧
      (m < (H - i).val → κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) < κ (i + (m : ZMod n) + 1)) := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero => intro _; simpa using And.intro hhigh (fun _ => hrise)
    | succ m ih =>
      intro hm
      have hm' : m < (H - i).val := by omega
      obtain ⟨hhighm, hrisem⟩ := ih hm'.le
      have hnext := hrisem hm'
      have hhigh' : level < κ (i + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n)) := by
        simpa [Nat.cast_add, add_assoc] using lt_trans hhighm hnext
      refine ⟨hhigh', fun hm'' => ?_⟩
      apply hstep _ (cyclic_offset_ne_of_lt_distance hm'') hhigh'
      simpa [Nat.cast_add, ← add_assoc] using hnext
  refine ⟨fun m hm => (hchain m hm).1, ?_⟩
  apply strictMonoOn_Iic_of_lt_succ
  intro m hm
  simpa [Nat.cast_add, add_assoc] using (hchain m hm.le).2 hm

blocks.tex:
(1) Prove by induction on $m\le d$ that $\lambda<\kappa_{i+m}$ and
  $\kappa_{i+m-1}<\kappa_{i+m}$.  For $m=0$ these are the hypotheses.  If
  they hold for $m<d$, then $i+m\ne H$ by \cref{lem:mt_cyclic_distance},
  so the propagation rule gives $\kappa_{i+m}<\kappa_{i+m+1}$.  Hence
  $\kappa_{i+m+1}$ is again above $\lambda$, and the incoming rise at
  $i+m+1$ is the step just proved.  The same step at each $m<d$ gives
  $\kappa_{i+m}<\kappa_{i+m+1}$, and consecutive strict increases on
  $\{0,\dots,d\}$ give strict monotonicity.

  (2) Here nothing is assumed about $\kappa_{i-1}$, so the invariant is
  changed: prove by induction that $\lambda<\kappa_{i+m}$ and, if $m<d$,
  $\kappa_{i+m}<\kappa_{i+m+1}$.  At $m=0$ the second clause is the
  outgoing rise.  Given the invariant at $m<d$, the step
  $\kappa_{i+m}<\kappa_{i+m+1}$ makes $\kappa_{i+m+1}$ high and is exactly an
  incoming rise at $i+m+1$; if $m+1<d$, then $i+m+1\ne H$ by
  \cref{lem:mt_cyclic_distance} and the propagation rule gives the next
  outgoing rise.  Monotonicity follows as before.  (If $d=0$, i.e.\ $i=H$,
  both conclusions are trivial.)

The induction runs for $d<n$ steps along the original cyclic word, so the
path never needs a bound on $n$ and never leaves the actual indices.

blocks.label: lem:mt_high_path
blocks.title: every high reading climbs to $H$
blocks.body:
Let $q$ be a highest secondary peak for $H$ in an adjacent-unequal word
  and $\kappa_q<\kappa_i$.  Then at least one of the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item (forward) with $d=\operatorname{val}(H-i)$, all $\kappa_{i+m}$,
      $m\le d$, are high and $m\mapsto\kappa_{i+m}$ is strictly increasing
      on $\{0,\dots,d\}$;
    \item (backward) with $d'=\operatorname{val}(i-H)$, all $\kappa_{i-m}$,
      $m\le d'$, are high and $m\mapsto\kappa_{i-m}$ is strictly increasing
      on $\{0,\dots,d'\}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  In either case the path ends at the literal index $H$
  (\cref{lem:mt_cyclic_distance}).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.high_path_to_global
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.high_path_to_global {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1)) (hhigh : κ q < κ i) :
    ((∀ m ≤ (H - i).val, κ q < κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (H - i).val)) ∨
    ((∀ m ≤ (i - H).val, κ q < κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (i - H).val)) := by
  by_cases hi : i = H
  · subst i
    left
    constructor
    · simpa using hhigh
    · intro a ha b hb hab
      simp only [sub_self, ZMod.val_zero, mem_Iic] at ha hb
      omega
  · rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne (hne i) with hrise | hfall
    · exact Or.inl (hq.forward_ascent_of_first_step hne hhigh hrise)
    · have hrise : κ i < κ (i - 1) := hq.backward_step hne hi hhigh hfall
      exact Or.inr (hq.backward_ascent_of_first_step hne hhigh hrise)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.backward_ascent
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.backward_ascent {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1))
    (hhigh : κ q < κ i) (hrise : κ (i + 1) < κ i) :
    (∀ m ≤ (i - H).val, κ q < κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (i - H).val) := by
  have hstep : ∀ j : ZMod n, j ≠ -H → κ q < κ (-j) →
      κ (-(j - 1)) < κ (-j) → κ (-j) < κ (-(j + 1)) := by
    intro j hj hh hr
    have hj' : -j ≠ H := by intro e; apply hj; simpa using congrArg Neg.neg e
    have hr' : κ (-j + 1) < κ (-j) := by simpa [neg_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hr
    simpa [neg_add, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hq.backward_step hne hj' hh hr'
  have hp := strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_rising (κ := fun j : ZMod n => κ (-j))
    (i := -i) (H := -H) hstep (by simpa using hhigh)
      (by simpa [neg_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hrise)
  simpa [neg_add, neg_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hp

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.forward_ascent_of_first_step
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.forward_ascent_of_first_step {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1))
    (hhigh : κ q < κ i) (hrise : κ i < κ (i + 1)) :
    (∀ m ≤ (H - i).val, κ q < κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (H - i).val) :=
  strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_first_step (fun _ => hq.forward_step hne) hhigh hrise

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.backward_ascent_of_first_step
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.backward_ascent_of_first_step {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1))
    (hhigh : κ q < κ i) (hrise : κ i < κ (i - 1)) :
    (∀ m ≤ (i - H).val, κ q < κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (i - H).val) := by
  have hstep : ∀ j : ZMod n, j ≠ -H → κ q < κ (-j) →
      κ (-(j - 1)) < κ (-j) → κ (-j) < κ (-(j + 1)) := by
    intro j hj hh hr
    have hj' : -j ≠ H := by intro e; apply hj; simpa using congrArg Neg.neg e
    have hr' : κ (-j + 1) < κ (-j) := by simpa [neg_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hr
    simpa [neg_add, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hq.backward_step hne hj' hh hr'
  have hp := strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_first_step (κ := fun j : ZMod n => κ (-j))
    (i := -i) (H := -H) hstep (by simpa using hhigh)
      (by simpa [neg_add, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hrise)
  simpa [neg_add, neg_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hp

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.forward_ascent
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.forward_ascent {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1))
    (hhigh : κ q < κ i) (hrise : κ (i - 1) < κ i) :
    (∀ m ≤ (H - i).val, κ q < κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (H - i).val) :=
  strictMonoOn_cyclicPath_of_rising (fun _ => hq.forward_step hne) hhigh hrise

deps.title: one step of a high path
deps.label: lem:mt_high_step

blocks.tex:
The forward step of \cref{lem:mt_high_step} is the propagation rule of
  \cref{lem:mt_cyclic_path} at level $\lambda=\kappa_q$; this gives the
  forward paths from an incoming or an outgoing rise.  For the backward
  paths apply \cref{lem:mt_cyclic_path} to the reflected word
  $j\mapsto\kappa_{-j}$ with marked index $-H$: its propagation rule is the
  backward step of \cref{lem:mt_high_step} at $-j\ne H$, and its forward
  path from $-i$ is the backward path from $i$, with
  $\operatorname{val}(-H-(-i))=\operatorname{val}(i-H)$.

  Now let $i$ be high.  If $i=H$, the forward path has $d=0$ and is the
  single high reading $\kappa_H$.  Otherwise compare $\kappa_i$ with
  $\kappa_{i+1}$, which differ.  If $\kappa_i<\kappa_{i+1}$, the forward
  path with an outgoing first rise applies.  If $\kappa_{i+1}<\kappa_i$, the
  backward step of \cref{lem:mt_high_step} (using $i\ne H$ and that $i$ is
  high) gives $\kappa_i<\kappa_{i-1}$, an outgoing first rise in the
  backward direction, and the backward path applies.  No hypothesis on the
  other neighbour of $i$ is needed in either case.

blocks.title: No wrapping and the single mountain

blocks.tex:
We now pass from cyclic paths to ordinary natural offsets from $q$.  The
point is that a high path can never pass through $q$ itself, because
$\kappa_q$ is not high.  Write $h=\operatorname{val}(H-q)$ for the offset of
the marked maximum; this index is unrelated to the curvature parameter $h$
of the native chapters.

blocks.label: lem:mt_no_wrap
blocks.title: high paths do not wrap past $q$
blocks.body:
Let $r=\operatorname{val}(i-q)$.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item If $\kappa_q<\kappa_{i+m}$ for all $m\le d=\operatorname{val}(H-i)$,
      then $r+d<n$ and $h=r+d$.
    \item If $\kappa_q<\kappa_{i-m}$ for all $m\le d'=\operatorname{val}(i-H)$,
      then $d'<r$ and $h=r-d'$.
  \end{enumerate}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.high_forward_path_offsets
lean.code:
theorem high_forward_path_offsets {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H q i : ZMod n}
    (hpath : ∀ m ≤ (H - i).val, κ q < κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) :
    (i - q).val + (H - i).val < n ∧
      (H - q).val = (i - q).val + (H - i).val := by
  have hi_lt := ZMod.val_lt (i - q)
  have hd_lt := ZMod.val_lt (H - i)
  have hsum : (i - q).val + (H - i).val < n := by
    by_contra h
    have hm : n - (i - q).val ≤ (H - i).val := by omega
    have heq : i + ((n - (i - q).val : ℕ) : ZMod n) = q := by
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hi_lt.le, ZMod.natCast_self, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
      ring
    have hh := hpath (n - (i - q).val) hm
    rw [heq] at hh
    exact lt_irrefl _ hh
  refine ⟨hsum, ?_⟩
  have hval := ZMod.val_add_of_lt hsum
  have heq : (i - q) + (H - i) = H - q := by ring
  rwa [heq] at hval

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.high_backward_path_offsets
lean.code:
theorem high_backward_path_offsets {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H q i : ZMod n}
    (hpath : ∀ m ≤ (i - H).val, κ q < κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) :
    (i - H).val < (i - q).val ∧
      (H - q).val = (i - q).val - (i - H).val := by
  have hlt : (i - H).val < (i - q).val := by
    by_contra h
    have hh := hpath (i - q).val (le_of_not_gt h)
    have heq : i - ((i - q).val : ZMod n) = q := by
      rw [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
      ring
    rw [heq] at hh
    exact lt_irrefl _ hh
  refine ⟨hlt, ?_⟩
  have hval := ZMod.val_sub hlt.le
  have heq : (i - q) - (i - H) = H - q := by ring
  rwa [heq] at hval

blocks.tex:
(1) Suppose $r+d\ge n$.  Then $m=n-r$ satisfies $m\le d$, and
  $i+m=i+n-(i-q)=q$ in $\ZMod n$.  The hypothesis at this $m$ reads
  $\kappa_q<\kappa_q$, which is absurd.  Hence $r+d<n$; the natural
  representative of the sum $(i-q)+(H-i)=H-q$ is then the natural sum, so
  $h=r+d$.

  (2) Suppose $d'\ge r$.  The hypothesis at $m=r$ concerns
  $i-r=i-(i-q)=q$, again giving $\kappa_q<\kappa_q$.  Hence $d'<r$, and the
  representative of $(i-q)-(i-H)=H-q$ is the natural difference $r-d'$.

blocks.label: lem:mt_high_interval
blocks.title: the high set is an interval of offsets
blocks.body:
Let $q$ be a highest secondary peak for $H$ in an adjacent-unequal word.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item If $i$ is high, $r=\operatorname{val}(i-q)$, and $j$ is a natural
      number between $\min(r,h)$ and $\max(r,h)$, then $q+j$ is high.
    \item If $a,b<n$, the readings at $q+a$ and $q+b$ are high, and
      $a\le j\le b$, then $q+j$ is high.
  \end{enumerate}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.high_interval_to_global
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.high_interval_to_global {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q i : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ j, κ j ≠ κ (j + 1)) (hhigh : κ q < κ i)
    {j : ℕ} (hjlo : min (i - q).val (H - q).val ≤ j)
    (hjhi : j ≤ max (i - q).val (H - q).val) :
    κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) := by
  rcases hq.high_path_to_global hne hhigh with ⟨hp, -⟩ | ⟨hp, -⟩
  · obtain ⟨-, hoff⟩ := high_forward_path_offsets hp
    have horder : (i - q).val ≤ (H - q).val := by omega
    rw [min_eq_left horder] at hjlo
    rw [max_eq_right horder] at hjhi
    have hm : j - (i - q).val ≤ (H - i).val := by omega
    have hh := hp (j - (i - q).val) hm
    have heq : i + ((j - (i - q).val : ℕ) : ZMod n) = q + (j : ZMod n) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hjlo, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
      ring
    rwa [heq] at hh
  · obtain ⟨hd, hoff⟩ := high_backward_path_offsets hp
    have horder : (H - q).val ≤ (i - q).val := by omega
    rw [min_eq_right horder] at hjlo
    rw [max_eq_left horder] at hjhi
    have hm : (i - q).val - j ≤ (i - H).val := by omega
    have hh := hp ((i - q).val - j) hm
    have heq : i - (((i - q).val - j : ℕ) : ZMod n) = q + (j : ZMod n) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hjhi, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
      ring
    rwa [heq] at hh

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.high_interval
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.high_interval {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) {a b j : ℕ}
    (ha : a < n) (hb : b < n)
    (haHigh : κ q < κ (q + (a : ZMod n)))
    (hbHigh : κ q < κ (q + (b : ZMod n))) (haj : a ≤ j) (hjb : j ≤ b) :
    κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) := by
  have haoff : (q + (a : ZMod n) - q).val = a := by
    simpa using ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt ha
  have hboff : (q + (b : ZMod n) - q).val = b := by
    simpa using ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt hb
  rcases le_total j (H - q).val with hjH | hHj
  · apply hq.high_interval_to_global hne haHigh
    · rw [haoff]; exact (min_le_left _ _).trans haj
    · exact hjH.trans (le_max_right _ _)
  · apply hq.high_interval_to_global hne hbHigh
    · exact (min_le_right _ _).trans hHj
    · rw [hboff]; exact hjb.trans (le_max_left _ _)

deps.title: high paths do not wrap past $q$
deps.label: lem:mt_no_wrap

blocks.tex:
(1) Take the path of \cref{lem:mt_high_path}.  In the forward case,
  \cref{lem:mt_no_wrap}(1) gives $h=r+d\ge r$, so $r\le j\le h$ and
  $j-r\le d$; the reading at $i+(j-r)=q+j$ lies on the path, hence is high.
  In the backward case, \cref{lem:mt_no_wrap}(2) gives $h=r-d'\le r$, so
  $h\le j\le r$ and $r-j\le d'$; the reading at $i-(r-j)=q+j$ lies on the
  path.  In both cases the identification of the indices uses that the
  cast of $r$ is $i-q$.

  (2) The offsets of $q+a$ and $q+b$ from $q$ are $a$ and $b$ because
  $a,b<n$.  If $j\le h$ apply (1) to $i=q+a$: then
  $\min(a,h)\le a\le j\le h\le\max(a,h)$.  If $h\le j$ apply (1) to $i=q+b$:
  then $\min(b,h)\le h\le j\le b\le\max(b,h)$.

blocks.label: lem:mt_legs
blocks.title: the rising and the falling legs
blocks.body:
Let $q$ be a highest secondary peak for $H$ in an adjacent-unequal word.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item If $a<b\le h$ and $q+a$ is high, then
      $\kappa_{q+a}<\kappa_{q+b}$.
    \item If $h\le a<b<n$ and $q+b$ is high, then
      $\kappa_{q+b}<\kappa_{q+a}$.
  \end{enumerate}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.rising_lt
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.rising_lt {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) {a b : ℕ}
    (hab : a < b) (hbH : b ≤ (H - q).val)
    (haHigh : κ q < κ (q + (a : ZMod n))) :
    κ (q + (a : ZMod n)) < κ (q + (b : ZMod n)) := by
  have ha : a < n := lt_trans hab (lt_of_le_of_lt hbH (ZMod.val_lt _))
  have haoff : (q + (a : ZMod n) - q).val = a := by
    simpa using ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt ha
  rcases hq.high_path_to_global hne haHigh with ⟨hp, hm⟩ | ⟨hp, -⟩
  · have hoff := (high_forward_path_offsets hp).2
    rw [haoff] at hoff
    have hmd : b - a ≤ (H - (q + (a : ZMod n))).val := by omega
    have hh := hm (show 0 ∈ Iic (H - (q + (a : ZMod n))).val by simp)
      hmd (show 0 < b - a by omega)
    have heq : q + (a : ZMod n) + ((b - a : ℕ) : ZMod n) = q + (b : ZMod n) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hab.le]
      ring
    simpa [heq] using hh
  · have hoff := (high_backward_path_offsets hp).2
    rw [haoff] at hoff
    omega

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.falling_lt
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.falling_lt {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) {a b : ℕ}
    (hHa : (H - q).val ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb : b < n)
    (hbHigh : κ q < κ (q + (b : ZMod n))) :
    κ (q + (b : ZMod n)) < κ (q + (a : ZMod n)) := by
  have hboff : (q + (b : ZMod n) - q).val = b := by
    simpa using ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt hb
  rcases hq.high_path_to_global hne hbHigh with ⟨hp, -⟩ | ⟨hp, hm⟩
  · have hoff := (high_forward_path_offsets hp).2
    rw [hboff] at hoff
    omega
  · obtain ⟨hd, hoff⟩ := high_backward_path_offsets hp
    rw [hboff] at hd hoff
    have hmd : b - a ≤ (q + (b : ZMod n) - H).val := by omega
    have hh := hm (show 0 ∈ Iic (q + (b : ZMod n) - H).val by simp)
      hmd (show 0 < b - a by omega)
    have heq : q + (b : ZMod n) - ((b - a : ℕ) : ZMod n) = q + (a : ZMod n) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hab.le]
      ring
    simpa [heq] using hh

deps.title: high paths do not wrap past $q$
deps.label: lem:mt_no_wrap

blocks.tex:
(1) Here $a<n$, so $\operatorname{val}((q+a)-q)=a$.  Take the path of
  \cref{lem:mt_high_path} from $i=q+a$.  In the backward case
  \cref{lem:mt_no_wrap}(2) would give $h=a-d'\le a<b\le h$, which is
  impossible: a high reading before $H$ cannot descend to $H$ the wrong way
  round.  So the forward case holds, and \cref{lem:mt_no_wrap}(1) gives
  $h=a+d$, whence $0<b-a\le d$.  Strict increase along the path from offset
  $0$ to offset $b-a$ gives $\kappa_{q+a}<\kappa_{q+a+(b-a)}=\kappa_{q+b}$.

  (2) Symmetrically, from $i=q+b$ (offset $b$) the forward case would give
  $h=b+d\ge b>a\ge h$, impossible.  So the backward case holds with
  $d'<b$ and $h=b-d'$, whence $0<b-a\le d'$, and strict increase along the
  backward path gives $\kappa_{q+b}<\kappa_{q+b-(b-a)}=\kappa_{q+a}$.

blocks.label: thm:mt_mountain
blocks.title: the single mountain above the secondary peak
blocks.body:
Let $q$ be a highest secondary peak for $H$ in an adjacent-unequal word,
  with $\kappa_q<\kappa_H$, and let $h=\operatorname{val}(H-q)$.  Then there
  are natural numbers $a,b$ with
  \[
    2\le a\le h\le b,\qquad b+2\le n,
  \]
  such that for every $j<n$
  \[
    \kappa_q<\kappa_{q+j}\iff a\le j\le b ,
  \]
  $j\mapsto\kappa_{q+j}$ is strictly increasing on $[a,h]$ and strictly
  decreasing on $[h,b]$.  Consequently, if $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$
  holds and $H$ is a strict unique global maximum ($\kappa_i<\kappa_H$ for
  $i\ne H$), then a highest secondary peak with such a mountain exists, and
  every high reading has a high monotone path to $H$ as in
  \cref{lem:mt_high_path}.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_secondaryPeak_with_high_paths
lean.code:
theorem exists_secondaryPeak_with_high_paths {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (H : ZMod n) (hglobal : ∀ i, i ≠ H → κ i < κ H) :
    ∃ q, HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q ∧ κ q < κ H ∧
      ∀ i, κ q < κ i →
        ((∀ m ≤ (H - i).val, κ q < κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) ∧
          StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i + (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (H - i).val)) ∨
        ((∀ m ≤ (i - H).val, κ q < κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) ∧
          StrictMonoOn (fun m : ℕ => κ (i - (m : ZMod n))) (Iic (i - H).val)) := by
  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := exists_highestSecondaryPeak hdfv hne H
  exact ⟨q, hq, hglobal q hq.ne_global, fun _ => hq.high_path_to_global hne⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.exists_mountain
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.exists_mountain {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) (hH : κ q < κ H) :
    ∃ a b : ℕ, 2 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ (H - q).val ∧ (H - q).val ≤ b ∧ b + 2 ≤ n ∧
      (∀ j < n, κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) ↔ a ≤ j ∧ j ≤ b) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun j : ℕ => κ (q + (j : ZMod n))) (Icc a (H - q).val) ∧
      StrictAntiOn (fun j : ℕ => κ (q + (j : ZMod n))) (Icc (H - q).val b) := by
  classical
  let s := (Finset.range n).filter (fun j : ℕ => κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)))
  have hmem : ∀ j, j ∈ s ↔ j < n ∧ κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) := by
    intro j; simp [s]
  have hHmem : (H - q).val ∈ s := by
    rw [hmem]
    refine ⟨ZMod.val_lt _, ?_⟩
    simpa [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val] using hH
  have hs : s.Nonempty := ⟨_, hHmem⟩
  let a := s.min' hs
  let b := s.max' hs
  have ha := (hmem a).mp (s.min'_mem hs)
  have hb := (hmem b).mp (s.max'_mem hs)
  have haH : a ≤ (H - q).val := s.min'_le _ hHmem
  have hHb : (H - q).val ≤ b := s.le_max' _ hHmem
  have ha2 : 2 ≤ a := by
    by_contra h
    have ha01 : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by omega
    rcases ha01 with ha0 | ha1
    · simpa [ha0] using ha.2
    · have hh : κ q < κ (q + 1) := by simpa [ha1] using ha.2
      exact (not_lt_of_gt hq.is_peak.2) hh
  have hb2 : b + 2 ≤ n := by
    by_contra h
    have hbn : b = n - 1 := by omega
    have hidx : q + (b : ZMod n) = q - 1 := by
      rw [hbn, Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ n), ZMod.natCast_self]
      simp [sub_eq_add_neg]
    have hh : κ q < κ (q - 1) := by simpa [hidx] using hb.2
    exact (not_lt_of_gt hq.is_peak.1) hh
  have hinterval : ∀ j < n, κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) ↔ a ≤ j ∧ j ≤ b := by
    intro j hj
    constructor
    · intro hh
      have hjmem := (hmem j).mpr ⟨hj, hh⟩
      exact ⟨s.min'_le _ hjmem, s.le_max' _ hjmem⟩
    · rintro ⟨haj, hjb⟩
      exact hq.high_interval hne ha.1 hb.1 ha.2 hb.2 haj hjb
  refine ⟨a, b, ha2, haH, hHb, hb2, hinterval, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i hi j hj hij
    rcases hi with ⟨hia, hiH⟩
    rcases hj with ⟨hja, hjH⟩
    apply hq.rising_lt hne hij hjH
    exact (hinterval i (by omega)).mpr ⟨hia, by omega⟩
  · intro i hi j hj hij
    rcases hi with ⟨hiH, hib⟩
    rcases hj with ⟨hjH, hjb⟩
    apply hq.falling_lt hne hiH hij (by omega)
    exact (hinterval j (by omega)).mpr ⟨by omega, hjb⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_secondaryPeak_mountain
lean.code:
theorem exists_secondaryPeak_mountain {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (H : ZMod n) (hglobal : ∀ i, i ≠ H → κ i < κ H) :
    ∃ q : ZMod n, ∃ a b : ℕ, HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q ∧
      2 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ (H - q).val ∧ (H - q).val ≤ b ∧ b + 2 ≤ n ∧
      (∀ j < n, κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) ↔ a ≤ j ∧ j ≤ b) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun j : ℕ => κ (q + (j : ZMod n))) (Icc a (H - q).val) ∧
      StrictAntiOn (fun j : ℕ => κ (q + (j : ZMod n))) (Icc (H - q).val b) := by
  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := exists_highestSecondaryPeak hdfv hne H
  obtain ⟨a, b, hab⟩ := hq.exists_mountain hne (hglobal q hq.ne_global)
  exact ⟨q, a, b, hq, hab⟩

deps.title: existence of the highest secondary peak
deps.label: lem:mt_secondary_exists

blocks.tex:
Let $S=\{j<n:\kappa_q<\kappa_{q+j}\}$.  It contains $h$, because the cast
  of $h$ is $H-q$ and $\kappa_q<\kappa_H$.  Let $a=\min S$ and $b=\max S$;
  then $a\le h\le b<n$.

  \emph{Bounds.}  $0\notin S$ since $\kappa_{q+0}=\kappa_q$, and $1\notin S$
  since $q$ is a strict local maximum, $\kappa_{q+1}<\kappa_q$.  Hence
  $a\ge2$.  If $b=n-1$ then $q+b=q-1$ in $\ZMod n$, and
  $\kappa_{q-1}<\kappa_q$ contradicts $b\in S$; hence $b\le n-2$.

  \emph{Interval.}  If $j<n$ is high then $a\le j\le b$ by definition of
  $\min$ and $\max$.  Conversely, if $a\le j\le b$ then $q+j$ is high by
  \cref{lem:mt_high_interval}(2) applied to the two high endpoints $a,b$.

  \emph{Legs.}  For $a\le i<j\le h$, the reading at $q+i$ is high by the
  interval property, so \cref{lem:mt_legs}(1) gives
  $\kappa_{q+i}<\kappa_{q+j}$.  For $h\le i<j\le b$, the reading at $q+j$ is
  high, so \cref{lem:mt_legs}(2) gives $\kappa_{q+j}<\kappa_{q+i}$.

  Either leg may have length zero: $a=h$ or $h=b$ is allowed, and nothing in
  the statement asserts a nontrivial rise.  The theorem needs only the
  selected-peak property, adjacent inequality and $\kappa_q<\kappa_H$.  For
  the combined statements, \cref{lem:mt_secondary_exists} selects $q$, and
  strict unique maximality at $H$ gives $\kappa_q<\kappa_H$ because $q\ne H$;
  the path statement is \cref{lem:mt_high_path}.

The theorem is exact on the original word: repeated nonadjacent readings,
low readings of arbitrary number and arbitrary values between $q$ and the
mountain are all retained.  The complementary offsets $0,\dots,a-1$ and
$b+1,\dots,n-1$ carry readings at most $\kappa_q$.

blocks.label: lem:mt_normalized_entry
blocks.title: the normalized low entry
blocks.body:
If $H\ne0$ in $\ZMod n$ then the cast of the natural number
  $\operatorname{val}(H)-1$ is $H-1$.  Now let $\mu$ be adjacent-unequal,
  let $0$ be a highest secondary peak for $H$, and let $\mu_0=1<\mu_H$.
  Put $h=\operatorname{val}(H)$ and take $a,b$ from \cref{thm:mt_mountain}.
  Then
  \[
    \mu_1<1,\quad \mu_{-1}=\mu_{n-1}<1,\quad
    \mu_{a-1}\le1<\mu_a,\quad 2\le a\le h,\quad h+2\le n,
  \]
  $j\mapsto\mu_j$ is strictly increasing on $[a,h]$, and the forward
  terminal flag $\Phi(\mu_1,\mu_{H-1},\mu_H,\mu_{-1})$ is the flag
  $\Phi(\mu_1,\mu_{h-1},\mu_h,\mu_{n-1})$ at the natural indices.  If this
  flag is nonnegative, then $a<h$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.natPred_val_residue
lean.code:
theorem natPred_val_residue [NeZero n] {j : ZMod n} (hj : j ≠ 0) :
    ((j.val - 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) = j - 1 := by
  have hv : 1 ≤ j.val := by
    have : j.val ≠ 0 := (ZMod.val_eq_zero j).not.mpr hj
    omega
  rw [Nat.cast_sub hv, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val, Nat.cast_one]

deps.title: a low entry forces a negative flag
deps.label: lem:nfp_flag_negative

blocks.tex:
$H\ne0$ gives $\operatorname{val}(H)\ge1$, so the natural subtraction is
  exact and its cast is $H-1$.  This premise matters: at $H=0$ the natural
  predecessor $0-1=0$ would not be the cyclic predecessor $-1$.  Here
  $H\ne0$ because the secondary peak $0$ differs from $H$.

  With $q=0$, \cref{thm:mt_mountain} gives $2\le a\le h\le b$ and
  $b+2\le n$, so $h+2\le n$, together with the rising leg on $[a,h]$.  Since
  $0$ is a strict local maximum with $\mu_0=1$, $\mu_1<1$ and $\mu_{-1}<1$;
  the cast of $n-1$ is $-1$.  The offset $a-1<a$ is not in $[a,b]$, so
  $\mu_{a-1}\le1$, while $a\in[a,b]$ gives $\mu_a>1$.  The two flags are
  literally equal after the index identifications
  ($\operatorname{val}(H)-1\mapsto H-1$, $n-1\mapsto-1$).

  Finally, if $a=h$ then $\mu_{h-1}=\mu_{a-1}\le1$ and $\mu_1<1$, so the
  terminal flag is negative by \cref{lem:nfp_flag_negative}.  Thus a
  nonnegative terminal forces a nontrivial rising leg; this is a consequence
  of the flag, not an assumption on the mountain.

  In the Lean development the displayed entry data are derived inline in
  the proof of
  \verb|HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_rising_terminal|
  (\cref{thm:nfp_rising_anchor}(3)), and the exclusion of $a=h$ is part of
  the selector \cref{lem:nfp_rising_transition}, whose least qualifying
  index cannot be $a-1$.

Recall the controller $C_F^\kappa=(Z,\tau)$ of \cref{def:four_active_controller}
for a frame $F$ and a word $\kappa$: with $s_j,t_j$ the literal start and
finish readings, $\alpha_j=\arcsin(s_jL_j)$, $\beta_j=\arcsin(t_jL_j)$ and the
grouped turns $\theta=(\Theta_0,\dots,\Theta_3)=F.\mathrm{turns}(\kappa,L)$,
\[
  Z=L_0+L_1u(\theta_1)+L_2u(\theta_1+\theta_2)+L_3u(\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3),
  \qquad \tau=\theta_0+\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3-2\pi,
\]
where $u(x)=e^{ix}$ and $L\in\RR^4$ are the four \emph{half}-lengths.  The
second component $\tau$ is a real lifted turn defect, not an angle modulo
$2\pi$.

blocks.label: lem:mt_scale_identity
blocks.title: exact scaling identities
blocks.body:
For every frame $F$, word $\kappa$, $s\in\RR$ and $L\in\RR^4$,
  \[
    F.\mathrm{turns}(\kappa,sL)=F.\mathrm{turns}(s\kappa,L),\qquad
    C_F^{\kappa}(sL)=\bigl(s\,Z_F^{s\kappa}(L),\ \tau_F^{s\kappa}(L)\bigr).
  \]
  Hence for $s\ne0$ and all $L$,
  $C_F^{s\kappa}(L)=\bigl(s^{-1}Z_F^{\kappa}(sL),\ \tau_F^{\kappa}(sL)\bigr)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.turns_scale_input
lean.code:
theorem turns_scale_input (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (s : ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    F.turns κ (s • L) = F.turns (fun i => s * κ i) L := by
  funext j
  fin_cases j <;>
    simp [turns, startArc, finishArc, start, finish, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
      mul_assoc, mul_left_comm, mul_comm]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller_scale
lean.code:
theorem controller_scale (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) {s : ℝ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    F.controller (fun i => s * κ i) L =
      (((s : ℂ)⁻¹) * (F.controller κ (s • L)).1, (F.controller κ (s • L)).2) := by
  rw [F.controller_scale_input]
  simp [hs]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller_scale_input
lean.code:
theorem controller_scale_input (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (s : ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    F.controller κ (s • L) =
      ((s : ℂ) * (F.controller (fun i => s * κ i) L).1,
        (F.controller (fun i => s * κ i) L).2) := by
  apply Prod.ext
  · simp only [controller, turns_scale_input, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Complex.ofReal_mul]
    ring
  · simp only [controller, turns_scale_input]

blocks.tex:
Each arcsine argument is a product of a literal reading and a half-length:
  $s_j\cdot(sL_j)=(ss_j)L_j$, and likewise for $t_j$.  So the eight arcsines,
  and hence the four turns and $\tau$, agree.  With equal turns, $Z$ is
  linear in the four length coefficients, so scaling $L$ by $s$ multiplies $Z$
  by $s$.  For $s\ne0$ apply this to $s\kappa$ and divide by $s$.  These
  identities hold for arbitrary signed $L$, not only on the zero set.

blocks.label: lem:mt_scale_deriv
blocks.title: derivative under scaling
blocks.body:
Let $s\ne0$ and let $C_F^\kappa$ be differentiable at $L$.  Then for all
  $v\in\RR^4$
  \[
    DC_F^{s\kappa}(s^{-1}L)\,v=
      \bigl(s^{-1}\,DZ_F^{\kappa}(L)(sv),\ D\tau_F^{\kappa}(L)(sv)\bigr).
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.fderiv_controller_scale
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_controller_scale {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {s : ℝ} (hs : s ≠ 0)
    {L : Fin 4 → ℝ} (hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (F.controller κ) L) (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    fderiv ℝ (F.controller (fun i => s * κ i)) (s⁻¹ • L) v =
      (((s : ℂ)⁻¹) * (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L (s • v)).1,
        (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L (s • v)).2) := by
  let S : (Fin 4 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (Fin 4 → ℝ) := s • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Fin 4 → ℝ)
  have hSL : S (s⁻¹ • L) = L := by simp [S, hs]
  have hd' : HasFDerivAt (F.controller κ) (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L)
      (S (s⁻¹ • L)) := by simpa only [hSL] using hd.hasFDerivAt
  have hf := hd'.comp (s⁻¹ • L) S.hasFDerivAt
  have hprod := (hf.fst.const_mul ((s : ℂ)⁻¹)).prodMk hf.snd
  have hfun : (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ =>
      (((s : ℂ)⁻¹) * (F.controller κ (S X)).1, (F.controller κ (S X)).2)) =
      F.controller (fun i => s * κ i) := by
    funext X
    simpa [S] using (F.controller_scale κ hs X).symm
  change HasFDerivAt (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ =>
      (((s : ℂ)⁻¹) * (F.controller κ (S X)).1, (F.controller κ (S X)).2)) _ _ at hprod
  rw [hfun] at hprod
  rw [hprod.fderiv]
  simp [S, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, smul_eq_mul]

end FourActiveSlots.Frame

namespace RegularFourAnchor

variable {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}

blocks.tex:
By \cref{lem:mt_scale_identity}, $C_F^{s\kappa}=\Lambda\circ C_F^\kappa\circ S$,
  where $S(X)=sX$ is linear with $S(s^{-1}L)=L$ and
  $\Lambda(z,t)=(s^{-1}z,t)$ is real linear.  The chain rule at $s^{-1}L$
  gives the formula, and uniqueness of the Fr\'echet derivative identifies it
  with $DC_F^{s\kappa}(s^{-1}L)$.

blocks.label: lem:mt_anchor_differentiable
blocks.title: surjectivity forces differentiability
blocks.body:
For every regular four-edge anchor $(F,L)$ of $\kappa$, the controller
  $C_F^\kappa$ is differentiable at $L$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.differentiableAt_controller
lean.code:
theorem differentiableAt_controller (A : RegularFourAnchor κ) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (A.frame.controller κ) A.halfLengths := by
  by_contra h
  have hs := A.regular
  rw [fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt h] at hs
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hs (0, 1)
  have := congrArg Prod.snd hv
  norm_num at this

blocks.tex:
In Lean the Fr\'echet derivative of a function at a point where it is not
  differentiable is defined to be $0$.  The zero map
  $\RR^4\to\CC\times\RR$ does not hit $(0,1)$, so surjectivity of
  $DC_F^\kappa(L)$ rules out nondifferentiability.  This is a formal
  convenience only: the transports below still prove differentiability of
  the individual turns (\cref{lem:mt_turn_differentiable}) where the product
  and chain rules require it.

blocks.label: lem:mt_anchor_scale
blocks.title: positive rescaling of an anchor
blocks.body:
If $(F,L)$ is a regular anchor of $\kappa$ and $s>0$, then $(F,s^{-1}L)$ is
  a regular anchor of $s\kappa$.  The four actual edges are unchanged.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.scale
lean.code:
noncomputable def scale (A : RegularFourAnchor κ) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    RegularFourAnchor (fun i => s * κ i) where
  frame := A.frame
  halfLengths := s⁻¹ • A.halfLengths
  positive j := mul_pos (inv_pos.mpr hs) (A.positive j)
  start_lt := by
    intro j
    have hproduct : A.frame.start (fun i => s * κ i) j * (s⁻¹ • A.halfLengths) j =
        A.frame.start κ j * A.halfLengths j := by
      simp [Frame.start, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hs.ne', mul_assoc, mul_left_comm]
    rw [hproduct]
    exact A.start_lt j
  finish_lt := by
    intro j
    have hproduct : A.frame.finish (fun i => s * κ i) j * (s⁻¹ • A.halfLengths) j =
        A.frame.finish κ j * A.halfLengths j := by
      simp [Frame.finish, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hs.ne', mul_assoc, mul_left_comm]
    rw [hproduct]
    exact A.finish_lt j
  zero := by
    rw [A.frame.controller_scale κ hs.ne']
    simp [hs.ne', A.zero]
  regular := by
    intro y
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := A.regular ((s : ℂ) * y.1, y.2)
    refine ⟨s⁻¹ • v, ?_⟩
    rw [A.frame.fderiv_controller_scale hs.ne' A.differentiableAt_controller]
    simp [hs.ne', hv]

blocks.tex:
\emph{Positivity and guards.}  $s^{-1}L_j>0$.  The start product for
  $s\kappa$ is $(s\,s_j)(s^{-1}L_j)=s_jL_j<1$, and likewise for the four
  finish products: the eight guards are literally the old ones.

  \emph{Zero.}  By \cref{lem:mt_scale_identity},
  $C_F^{s\kappa}(s^{-1}L)=(s^{-1}Z_F^\kappa(L),\tau_F^\kappa(L))=(0,0)$.

  \emph{Surjectivity.}  $C_F^\kappa$ is differentiable at $L$ by
  \cref{lem:mt_anchor_differentiable}, so \cref{lem:mt_scale_deriv} applies.
  Given a target $(y_1,y_2)$, choose $v$ with
  $DC_F^\kappa(L)v=(s\,y_1,y_2)$.  Then
  $DC_F^{s\kappa}(s^{-1}L)(s^{-1}v)=(s^{-1}\cdot s\,y_1,\,y_2)=(y_1,y_2)$.
  Thus the derivative is the old derivative composed with the invertible
  input scaling and followed by the invertible output map $(z,t)\mapsto(s^{-1}z,t)$,
  and the preimage is explicit.

blocks.label: def:mt_slot_perm
blocks.title: slot rotation, reversal and the slot controller
blocks.body:
For $v\in\alpha^4$ put
  \[
    \operatorname{rot}v=(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_0),\qquad
    \operatorname{rev}v=(v_3,v_2,v_1,v_0).
  \]
  On $\RR^4$ both are continuous linear maps (coordinate permutations).  For
  $L,\theta\in\RR^4$ the \emph{slot controller} is
  \[
    \mathcal S(L,\theta)=\Bigl(L_0+L_1u(\theta_1)+L_2u(\theta_1+\theta_2)
      +L_3u(\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3),\
      \theta_0+\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3-2\pi\Bigr),
  \]
  so that $C_F^\kappa(L)=\mathcal S(L,F.\mathrm{turns}(\kappa,L))$ by
  definition.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.rotateFourCLM
lean.code:
noncomputable def rotateFourCLM : (Fin 4 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (Fin 4 → ℝ) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.pi fun j =>
    ContinuousLinearMap.proj (R := ℝ) (φ := fun _ : Fin 4 => ℝ)
      (![1, 2, 3, 0] j)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.reverseFour
lean.code: def reverseFour {α : Type*} (v : Fin 4 → α) : Fin 4 → α := ![v 3, v 2, v 1, v 0]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.rotateFourCLM_apply
lean.code:
@[simp] theorem rotateFourCLM_apply (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) : rotateFourCLM v = rotateFour v := by
  ext j
  fin_cases j <;> rfl

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.reverseFourCLM
lean.code:
noncomputable def reverseFourCLM : (Fin 4 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (Fin 4 → ℝ) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.pi fun j =>
    ContinuousLinearMap.proj (R := ℝ) (φ := fun _ : Fin 4 => ℝ)
      (![3, 2, 1, 0] j)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.reverseFourCLM_apply
lean.code:
@[simp] theorem reverseFourCLM_apply (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) : reverseFourCLM v = reverseFour v := by
  ext j
  fin_cases j <;> rfl

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.slotController
lean.code:
noncomputable def slotController (L θ : Fin 4 → ℝ) : ℂ × ℝ :=
  ((L 0 : ℂ) + (L 1 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1) +
    (L 2 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2) +
    (L 3 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3),
    θ 0 + θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3 - 2 * Real.pi)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.rotateFour
lean.code: def rotateFour {α : Type*} (v : Fin 4 → α) : Fin 4 → α := ![v 1, v 2, v 3, v 0]

blocks.tex:
Under rotation the edge slots become $(1,2,3,0)$ and the corner turns rotate
in the same way.  Under reversal the edge slots become $(3,2,1,0)$, but the
corners are reversed as $(0,3,2,1)$: corner $\theta_0$ lies between edges $3$
and $0$, which are again the last and the first edge after reversal.

blocks.label: lem:mt_slot_identities
blocks.title: exact slot identities
blocks.body:
For all $L,\theta\in\RR^4$, writing $\mathcal S(L,\theta)=(Z,\tau)$,
  \[
    \mathcal S(\operatorname{rot}L,\operatorname{rot}\theta)
      =\Bigl(u(-\theta_1)\bigl[Z+L_0\,(u(\tau)-1)\bigr],\ \tau\Bigr),
  \]
  \[
    \mathcal S\bigl(\operatorname{rev}L,(\theta_0,\theta_3,\theta_2,\theta_1)\bigr)
      =\Bigl(u(\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3)\,\overline{Z},\ \tau\Bigr).
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.slotController_reverse
lean.code:
theorem slotController_reverse (L θ : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    slotController (reverseFour L) ![θ 0, θ 3, θ 2, θ 1] =
      (unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3) * starRingEnd ℂ (slotController L θ).1,
        (slotController L θ).2) := by
  apply Prod.ext
  · have h1 : unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3) * unitPhase (-(θ 1)) =
        unitPhase (θ 3 + θ 2) := by
      rw [← unitPhase_add]; congr 1; ring
    have h2 : unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3) * unitPhase (-(θ 1 + θ 2)) =
        unitPhase (θ 3) := by
      rw [← unitPhase_add]; congr 1; ring
    have h3 : unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3) * unitPhase (-(θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3)) = 1 := by
      rw [← unitPhase_add]; simp [unitPhase]
    simp only [slotController, reverseFour, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
      Matrix.cons_val, Fin.isValue, map_add, map_mul, Complex.conj_ofReal, conjugate_phase]
    rw [show θ 3 + θ 2 + θ 1 = θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3 by ring]
    linear_combination -(L 1 : ℂ) * h1 - (L 2 : ℂ) * h2 - (L 3 : ℂ) * h3
  · simp only [slotController, reverseFour, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
      Matrix.cons_val, Fin.isValue]
    ring

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.slotController_rotate
lean.code:
theorem slotController_rotate (L θ : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    slotController (rotateFour L) (rotateFour θ) =
      (unitPhase (-(θ 1)) * ((slotController L θ).1 +
          (L 0 : ℂ) * (unitPhase ((slotController L θ).2) - 1)),
        (slotController L θ).2) := by
  apply Prod.ext
  · have hmul : unitPhase (θ 1) * (slotController (rotateFour L) (rotateFour θ)).1 =
        (slotController L θ).1 +
          (L 0 : ℂ) * (unitPhase ((slotController L θ).2) - 1) := by
      simp only [slotController, rotateFour, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
        Matrix.cons_val, Fin.isValue, unitPhase_sub_period, unitPhase_add]
      ring
    have hh := congrArg (fun z : ℂ => unitPhase (-(θ 1)) * z) hmul
    simpa only [← mul_assoc, unitPhase_neg_cancel, one_mul] using hh
  · simp only [slotController, rotateFour, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
      Matrix.cons_val, Fin.isValue]
    ring

deps.title: slot rotation, reversal and the slot controller
deps.label: def:mt_slot_perm

blocks.tex:
The turn components are sums of the same four $\theta_j$ in both cases.

  \emph{Rotation.}  The rotated closure is
  $Z'=L_1+L_2u(\theta_2)+L_3u(\theta_2+\theta_3)+L_0u(\theta_2+\theta_3+\theta_0)$.
  Multiplying by $u(\theta_1)$ and using $u(x)u(y)=u(x+y)$,
  \[
    u(\theta_1)Z'=L_1u(\theta_1)+L_2u(\theta_1+\theta_2)
      +L_3u(\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3)+L_0u(\tau+2\pi)
    =Z-L_0+L_0u(\tau),
  \]
  by $2\pi$-periodicity of $u$.  Multiplying by $u(-\theta_1)=u(\theta_1)^{-1}$
  gives the formula.  The four complex edge terms are only reordered; the
  term of the old edge $0$ now carries the full turn, and its phase differs
  from $1$ by $u(\tau)-1$.  Off the zero set of $\tau$ this correction is
  genuinely present, and it is kept.

  \emph{Reversal.}  The reversed closure is
  $L_3+L_2u(\theta_3)+L_1u(\theta_3+\theta_2)+L_0u(\theta_3+\theta_2+\theta_1)$.
  On the other hand $\overline{u(x)}=u(-x)$, so with
  $\sigma=\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3$
  \[
    u(\sigma)\overline{Z}=L_0u(\sigma)+L_1u(\sigma-\theta_1)
      +L_2u(\sigma-\theta_1-\theta_2)+L_3u(0),
  \]
  which is the same sum.

blocks.label: lem:mt_frame_identities
blocks.title: frame versions with literal endpoints
blocks.body:
Let $F$ be a frame of size $m$ for $\mu$ and $G$ a frame of size $n$ for
  $\kappa$, and write $\theta=F.\mathrm{turns}(\mu,L)$ and
  $C_F^\mu(L)=(Z,\tau)$.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item If $\operatorname{start}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{rot}(\operatorname{start}^F_\mu)$
      and $\operatorname{finish}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{rot}(\operatorname{finish}^F_\mu)$,
      then $G.\mathrm{turns}(\kappa,\operatorname{rot}L)=\operatorname{rot}\theta$ and
      \[
        C_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rot}L)
          =\bigl(u(-\theta_1)[Z+L_0(u(\tau)-1)],\ \tau\bigr).
      \]
    \item If $\operatorname{start}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{rev}(\operatorname{finish}^F_\mu)$
      and $\operatorname{finish}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{rev}(\operatorname{start}^F_\mu)$
      (reversed and swapped), then
      $G.\mathrm{turns}(\kappa,\operatorname{rev}L)=(\theta_0,\theta_3,\theta_2,\theta_1)$ and
      \[
        C_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rev}L)
          =\bigl(u(\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3)\,\overline{Z},\ \tau\bigr).
      \]
  \end{enumerate}
  Both hold for all $L\in\RR^4$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller_reverse_of_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem controller_reverse_of_endpoints {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : Frame m} {G : Frame n}
    (hstart : G.start κ = reverseFour (F.finish μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = reverseFour (F.start μ)) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    G.controller κ (reverseFour L) =
      (unitPhase ((F.turns μ L) 1 + (F.turns μ L) 2 + (F.turns μ L) 3) *
          starRingEnd ℂ (F.controller μ L).1, (F.controller μ L).2) := by
  change slotController (reverseFour L) (G.turns κ (reverseFour L)) = _
  rw [turns_reverse_of_endpoints hstart hfinish]
  exact slotController_reverse L (F.turns μ L)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.turns_reverse_of_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem turns_reverse_of_endpoints {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : Frame m} {G : Frame n}
    (hstart : G.start κ = reverseFour (F.finish μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = reverseFour (F.start μ)) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    G.turns κ (reverseFour L) =
      ![(F.turns μ L) 0, (F.turns μ L) 3, (F.turns μ L) 2, (F.turns μ L) 1] := by
  funext j
  fin_cases j <;> simp [turns, startArc, finishArc, hstart, hfinish, reverseFour, add_comm]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.turns_rotate_of_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem turns_rotate_of_endpoints {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : Frame m} {G : Frame n}
    (hstart : G.start κ = rotateFour (F.start μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = rotateFour (F.finish μ)) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    G.turns κ (rotateFour L) = rotateFour (F.turns μ L) := by
  funext j
  fin_cases j <;> simp [turns, startArc, finishArc, hstart, hfinish, rotateFour]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller_rotate_of_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem controller_rotate_of_endpoints {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : Frame m} {G : Frame n}
    (hstart : G.start κ = rotateFour (F.start μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = rotateFour (F.finish μ)) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    G.controller κ (rotateFour L) =
      (unitPhase (-((F.turns μ L) 1)) * ((F.controller μ L).1 +
          (L 0 : ℂ) * (unitPhase ((F.controller μ L).2) - 1)),
        (F.controller μ L).2) := by
  change slotController (rotateFour L) (G.turns κ (rotateFour L)) = _
  rw [turns_rotate_of_endpoints hstart hfinish]
  exact slotController_rotate L (F.turns μ L)

blocks.tex:
(1) The $G$-turn at corner $0$ is
  $\arcsin(t^G_3(\operatorname{rot}L)_3)+\arcsin(s^G_0(\operatorname{rot}L)_0)
   =\arcsin(t^F_0L_0)+\arcsin(s^F_1L_1)=\theta_1$,
  and the other three corners are checked in the same way.  Then
  $C_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rot}L)=\mathcal S(\operatorname{rot}L,\operatorname{rot}\theta)$
  and \cref{lem:mt_slot_identities} applies.

  (2) Now the start readings of $G$ are the reversed finish readings of $F$.
  At corner $0$:
  $\arcsin(t^G_3(\operatorname{rev}L)_3)+\arcsin(s^G_0(\operatorname{rev}L)_0)
   =\arcsin(s^F_0L_0)+\arcsin(t^F_3L_3)=\theta_0$;
  at corner $1$:
  $\arcsin(t^G_0L_3)+\arcsin(s^G_1L_2)=\arcsin(s^F_3L_3)+\arcsin(t^F_2L_2)=\theta_3$;
  and similarly corners $2,3$ give $\theta_2,\theta_1$.  The swap of start and
  finish is exactly what makes each corner reappear with both of its arcsine
  terms.  Then \cref{lem:mt_slot_identities} applies.

blocks.label: lem:mt_turn_differentiable
blocks.title: differentiability of turns and controller
blocks.body:
Let $L_j>0$, $s_j,t_j>0$, and $s_jL_j<1$, $t_jL_j<1$ for all $j$.  Then each
  turn $X\mapsto F.\mathrm{turns}(\kappa,X)_j$ and the controller $C_F^\kappa$
  are differentiable at $L$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.differentiableAt_turns_of_strict
lean.code:
theorem differentiableAt_turns_of_strict {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (F : Frame n) {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hL : ∀ j, 0 < L j)
    (hspos : ∀ j, 0 < F.start κ j) (hfpos : ∀ j, 0 < F.finish κ j)
    (hs : ∀ j, F.start κ j * L j < 1) (hf : ∀ j, F.finish κ j * L j < 1) :
    ∀ j, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun X => F.turns κ X j) L := by
  have hsa (j) : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun X => F.startArc κ X j) L := by
    apply (Real.differentiableAt_arcsin.mpr ?_).comp L
      (show DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ => F.start κ j * X j) L by fun_prop)
    exact ⟨by linarith [mul_pos (hspos j) (hL j)], ne_of_lt (hs j)⟩
  have hfa (j) : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun X => F.finishArc κ X j) L := by
    apply (Real.differentiableAt_arcsin.mpr ?_).comp L

  intro j
  fin_cases j

  · exact (hfa 0).add (hsa 1)
  · exact (hfa 1).add (hsa 2)
  · exact (hfa 2).add (hsa 3)

blocks.title: derivatives of the permuted controllers at a zero
blocks.body:
In the situation of \cref{lem:mt_frame_identities}, assume $C_F^\mu(L)=0$,
  that $C_F^\mu$ is differentiable at $L$, that $C_G^\kappa$ is
  differentiable at the permuted lengths, and that the turns
  $\theta_1$ (for rotation), respectively $\theta_1,\theta_2,\theta_3$ (for
  reversal), are differentiable at $L$.  Let $v\in\RR^4$ and
  $DC_F^\mu(L)v=(z,t)$.  Then
  \[
    DC_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rot}L)(\operatorname{rot}v)
      =\bigl(u(-\theta_1)\,(z+i\,L_0\,t),\ t\bigr)
  \]
  in case (1), and in case (2)
  \[
    DC_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rev}L)(\operatorname{rev}v)
      =\bigl(u(\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3)\,\overline{z},\ t\bigr).
  \]

lean.code:
theorem fderiv_controller_reverse_of_endpoints
    {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : Frame m} {G : Frame n} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hstart : G.start κ = reverseFour (F.finish μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = reverseFour (F.start μ))
    (hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (F.controller μ) L)
    (ht : ∀ j, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun X => F.turns μ X j) L)
    (hdG : DifferentiableAt ℝ (G.controller κ) (reverseFour L))
    (hz : F.controller μ L = 0) (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    fderiv ℝ (G.controller κ) (reverseFour L) (reverseFour v) =
      (unitPhase (F.turns μ L 1 + F.turns μ L 2 + F.turns μ L 3) *
        starRingEnd ℂ ((fderiv ℝ (F.controller μ) L v).1),
        (fderiv ℝ (F.controller μ) L v).2) := by
  have hp := phase_hasFDerivAt (((ht 1).hasFDerivAt.add (ht 2).hasFDerivAt).add
    (ht 3).hasFDerivAt)
  have hconj := Complex.conjCLE.toContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt.comp L hd.hasFDerivAt.fst
  have he := (hp.mul hconj).prodMk hd.hasFDerivAt.snd
  have hfun : (fun X =>
      (unitPhase (F.turns μ X 1 + F.turns μ X 2 + F.turns μ X 3) *
        starRingEnd ℂ (F.controller μ X).1, (F.controller μ X).2)) =
      fun X => G.controller κ (reverseFour X) := by
    funext X
    exact (controller_reverse_of_endpoints hstart hfinish X).symm
  change HasFDerivAt (fun X =>
      (unitPhase (F.turns μ X 1 + F.turns μ X 2 + F.turns μ X 3) *
        starRingEnd ℂ (F.controller μ X).1, (F.controller μ X).2)) _ L at he
  rw [hfun] at he
  have hrev : HasFDerivAt reverseFour reverseFourCLM L := by
    have hrfun : (reverseFourCLM : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → (Fin 4 → ℝ)) = reverseFour :=
      funext reverseFourCLM_apply
    rw [← hrfun]
    exact reverseFourCLM.hasFDerivAt
  have hc := hdG.hasFDerivAt.comp L hrev
  have hdEq := he.unique hc
  have hh := congrArg (fun D : (Fin 4 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (ℂ × ℝ) => D v) hdEq
  symm at hh
  simpa [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, hz, mul_assoc] using hh

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.fderiv_controller_rotate_of_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_controller_rotate_of_endpoints
    {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : Frame m} {G : Frame n} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hstart : G.start κ = rotateFour (F.start μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = rotateFour (F.finish μ))
    (hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (F.controller μ) L)
    (ht : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun X => F.turns μ X 1) L)
    (hdG : DifferentiableAt ℝ (G.controller κ) (rotateFour L))
    (hz : F.controller μ L = 0) (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    fderiv ℝ (G.controller κ) (rotateFour L) (rotateFour v) =
      (unitPhase (-(F.turns μ L 1)) *
        ((fderiv ℝ (F.controller μ) L v).1 +
          (L 0 : ℂ) * Complex.I * ((fderiv ℝ (F.controller μ) L v).2 : ℂ)),
        (fderiv ℝ (F.controller μ) L v).2) := by
  have hp := phase_hasFDerivAt ht.hasFDerivAt.neg
  have hτ := phase_hasFDerivAt hd.hasFDerivAt.snd
  have hL0 := Complex.ofRealCLM.hasFDerivAt.comp L
    (hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 4 => ℝ) 0 L)
  have he := (hp.mul (hd.hasFDerivAt.fst.add (hL0.mul (hτ.sub_const 1)))).prodMk
    hd.hasFDerivAt.snd
  have hfun : (fun X =>
      (unitPhase (-(F.turns μ X 1)) * ((F.controller μ X).1 +
        (X 0 : ℂ) * (unitPhase ((F.controller μ X).2) - 1)),
        (F.controller μ X).2)) = fun X => G.controller κ (rotateFour X) := by
    funext X
    exact (controller_rotate_of_endpoints hstart hfinish X).symm
  change HasFDerivAt (fun X =>
      (unitPhase (-(F.turns μ X 1)) * ((F.controller μ X).1 +
        (X 0 : ℂ) * (unitPhase ((F.controller μ X).2) - 1)),
        (F.controller μ X).2)) _ L at he
  rw [hfun] at he
  have hrot : HasFDerivAt rotateFour rotateFourCLM L := by
    have hrfun : (rotateFourCLM : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → (Fin 4 → ℝ)) = rotateFour :=
      funext rotateFourCLM_apply
    rw [← hrfun]
    exact rotateFourCLM.hasFDerivAt
  have hc := hdG.hasFDerivAt.comp L hrot
  have hdEq := he.unique hc
  have hh := congrArg (fun D : (Fin 4 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (ℂ × ℝ) => D v) hdEq
  symm at hh
  simpa [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, hz, unitPhase, mul_assoc, mul_add] using hh

deps.title: slot rotation, reversal and the slot controller
deps.label: def:mt_slot_perm

blocks.tex:
\emph{Rotation.}  By \cref{lem:mt_frame_identities}(1),
  $C_G^\kappa\circ\operatorname{rot}$ equals, as a function of $X$,
  \[
    X\longmapsto\Bigl(u(-\theta_1(X))\bigl[Z(X)+X_0\,(u(\tau(X))-1)\bigr],\ \tau(X)\Bigr).
  \]
  Differentiate the right side at $L$ by the product and chain rules, using
  $D[u\circ f]=i\,u(f)\,Df$.  At $L$ we have $Z(L)=0$ and $\tau(L)=0$.  Then:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item the derivative of the variable gauge $u(-\theta_1(X))$ multiplies
      the bracket at $L$, which is $0+L_0(u(0)-1)=0$;
    \item the derivative of the coefficient $X_0$ multiplies
      $u(\tau(L))-1=u(0)-1=0$;
    \item the derivative of $u(\tau(X))$ is $i\,u(0)\,t=i\,t$, multiplied by
      $L_0$: this term \emph{survives}.
  \end{itemize}
  Hence the derivative in direction $v$ is
  $\bigl(u(-\theta_1)(z+iL_0t),\,t\bigr)$.  The left side is differentiated by
  the chain rule through the linear map $\operatorname{rot}$, so it is
  $DC_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rot}L)(\operatorname{rot}v)$, and uniqueness of
  the derivative identifies both.

  \emph{Reversal.}  By \cref{lem:mt_frame_identities}(2),
  $C_G^\kappa\circ\operatorname{rev}$ is
  $X\mapsto\bigl(u(\sigma(X))\,\overline{Z(X)},\tau(X)\bigr)$ with
  $\sigma=\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3$.  Complex conjugation is real linear.
  The derivative of the varying phase multiplies $\overline{Z(L)}=0$, so
  only $u(\sigma(L))\,\overline{z}$ remains.  Uniqueness through
  $\operatorname{rev}$ gives the formula.

The two output maps $(z,t)\mapsto(u(-\theta_1)(z+iL_0t),t)$ and
$(z,t)\mapsto(u(\sigma)\overline z,t)$ are invertible \emph{real} linear maps
of $\CC\times\RR$.  For a target $(w,t)$ their preimages are
\[
  \bigl(u(\theta_1)w-i\,L_0\,t,\ t\bigr)
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \bigl(\overline{u(-\sigma)\,w},\ t\bigr),
\]
respectively.

blocks.label: thm:mt_reembed
blocks.title: reembedding under rotated or reflected endpoints
blocks.body:
Let $(F,L)$ be a regular anchor of a positive word $\mu$ and let $G$ be a
  frame of size $n$ for $\kappa$.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item If $G$ has rotated endpoints as in \cref{lem:mt_frame_identities}(1),
      then $(G,\operatorname{rot}L)$ is a regular anchor of $\kappa$.
    \item If $G$ has reversed and swapped endpoints as in
      \cref{lem:mt_frame_identities}(2), then $(G,\operatorname{rev}L)$ is a
      regular anchor of $\kappa$.
  \end{enumerate}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.reverseReembed
lean.code:
noncomputable def reverseReembed {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (A : RegularFourAnchor μ) (hμ : ∀ i, 0 < μ i) (G : Frame n)
    (hstart : G.start κ = reverseFour (A.frame.finish μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = reverseFour (A.frame.start μ)) :
    RegularFourAnchor κ := by
  have hL : ∀ j, 0 < reverseFour A.halfLengths j := by
    intro j
    fin_cases j <;> exact A.positive _
  have hs : ∀ j, G.start κ j * reverseFour A.halfLengths j < 1 := by
    intro j
    rw [hstart]
    fin_cases j <;> exact A.finish_lt _
  have hf : ∀ j, G.finish κ j * reverseFour A.halfLengths j < 1 := by
    intro j
    rw [hfinish]
    fin_cases j <;> exact A.start_lt _
  have hspos : ∀ j, 0 < G.start κ j := by
    intro j
    rw [hstart]
    fin_cases j <;> exact hμ _
  have hfpos : ∀ j, 0 < G.finish κ j := by
    intro j
    rw [hfinish]
    fin_cases j <;> exact hμ _
  have hdG := G.differentiableAt_controller_of_strict hL hspos hfpos hs hf
  have ht := A.frame.differentiableAt_turns_of_strict A.positive
    (fun j => hμ _) (fun j => hμ _) A.start_lt A.finish_lt
  refine ⟨G, reverseFour A.halfLengths, hL, hs, hf, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Frame.controller_reverse_of_endpoints hstart hfinish, A.zero]
    simp
  · intro y
    let θ := A.frame.turns μ A.halfLengths 1 + A.frame.turns μ A.halfLengths 2 +
      A.frame.turns μ A.halfLengths 3
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := A.regular (starRingEnd ℂ (unitPhase (-θ) * y.1), y.2)
    refine ⟨reverseFour v, ?_⟩
    rw [Frame.fderiv_controller_reverse_of_endpoints hstart hfinish
      A.differentiableAt_controller ht hdG A.zero, hv]
    have hc : unitPhase θ * unitPhase (-θ) = 1 := by
      rw [← unitPhase_add]
      simp [unitPhase]
    apply Prod.ext
    · change unitPhase θ * starRingEnd ℂ (starRingEnd ℂ (unitPhase (-θ) * y.1)) = y.1
      simp only [starRingEnd_apply, star_star]
      rw [← mul_assoc, hc, one_mul]
    · rfl

lean.code:
noncomputable def rotateReembed {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (A : RegularFourAnchor μ) (hμ : ∀ i, 0 < μ i) (G : Frame n)
    (hstart : G.start κ = rotateFour (A.frame.start μ))
    (hfinish : G.finish κ = rotateFour (A.frame.finish μ)) :
    RegularFourAnchor κ := by
  have hL : ∀ j, 0 < rotateFour A.halfLengths j := by
    intro j
    fin_cases j <;> exact A.positive _
  have hs : ∀ j, G.start κ j * rotateFour A.halfLengths j < 1 := by
    intro j
    rw [hstart]
    fin_cases j <;> exact A.start_lt _
  have hf : ∀ j, G.finish κ j * rotateFour A.halfLengths j < 1 := by
    intro j
    rw [hfinish]
    fin_cases j <;> exact A.finish_lt _
  have hspos : ∀ j, 0 < G.start κ j := by
    intro j
    rw [hstart]
    fin_cases j <;> exact hμ _
  have hfpos : ∀ j, 0 < G.finish κ j := by
    intro j
    rw [hfinish]
    fin_cases j <;> exact hμ _
  have hdG := G.differentiableAt_controller_of_strict hL hspos hfpos hs hf
  have ht := A.frame.differentiableAt_turns_of_strict A.positive
    (fun j => hμ _) (fun j => hμ _) A.start_lt A.finish_lt
  refine ⟨G, rotateFour A.halfLengths, hL, hs, hf, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Frame.controller_rotate_of_endpoints hstart hfinish, A.zero]
    simp [unitPhase]
  · intro y
    let θ := A.frame.turns μ A.halfLengths 1
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := A.regular
      (unitPhase θ * y.1 - (A.halfLengths 0 : ℂ) * Complex.I * (y.2 : ℂ), y.2)
    refine ⟨rotateFour v, ?_⟩
    rw [Frame.fderiv_controller_rotate_of_endpoints hstart hfinish
      A.differentiableAt_controller (ht 1) hdG A.zero, hv]
    have hc : unitPhase (-θ) * unitPhase θ = 1 := by
      rw [← unitPhase_add]
      simp [unitPhase]
    apply Prod.ext
    · change unitPhase (-θ) *
        ((unitPhase θ * y.1 - (A.halfLengths 0 : ℂ) * Complex.I * (y.2 : ℂ)) +
          (A.halfLengths 0 : ℂ) * Complex.I * (y.2 : ℂ)) = y.1
      rw [sub_add_cancel, ← mul_assoc, hc, one_mul]
    · rfl

deps.title: derivatives of the permuted controllers at a zero
deps.label: thm:mt_deriv_transport

blocks.tex:
\emph{Positivity and guards.}  The entries of $\operatorname{rot}L$ and
  $\operatorname{rev}L$ are those of $L$.  In case (1) the start guard of
  $G$ at slot $j$ is the start guard of $F$ at slot $j+1$, and similarly for
  finishes.  In case (2) the start guards of $G$ are the finish guards of $F$
  at the reversed slot, and vice versa.  So all eight guards transfer, and
  all eight endpoint readings of $G$ are readings of $\mu$, hence positive.

  \emph{Differentiability.}  By \cref{lem:mt_turn_differentiable},
  $C_G^\kappa$ is differentiable at the permuted lengths and every turn of
  $F$ is differentiable at $L$; $C_F^\mu$ is differentiable at $L$ by
  \cref{lem:mt_anchor_differentiable}.

  \emph{Zero.}  By the full identities of \cref{lem:mt_frame_identities} at
  $L$, where $Z=0$ and $\tau=0$:
  $C_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rot}L)=(u(-\theta_1)[0+L_0(u(0)-1)],0)=0$ and
  $C_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rev}L)=(u(\sigma)\overline0,0)=0$.

  \emph{Surjectivity.}  Let $(w,t)$ be a target.  In case (1) choose $v$ with
  $DC_F^\mu(L)v=(u(\theta_1)w-iL_0t,\,t)$ by regularity of $(F,L)$.  By
  \cref{thm:mt_deriv_transport},
  \[
    DC_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rot}L)(\operatorname{rot}v)
      =\bigl(u(-\theta_1)(u(\theta_1)w-iL_0t+iL_0t),\,t\bigr)=(w,t).
  \]
  In case (2) choose $v$ with $DC_F^\mu(L)v=(\overline{u(-\sigma)w},\,t)$;
  then
  $DC_G^\kappa(\operatorname{rev}L)(\operatorname{rev}v)
   =(u(\sigma)\,u(-\sigma)\,w,\,t)=(w,t)$.

  Equality of zero sets alone would not transport rank; the derivatives are
  related by the explicit invertible maps above, with inputs related by the
  slot permutations.  No additional dormant edge is used to supply rank.

blocks.body:
Let $F$ have edges $e_0<e_1<e_2<e_3<n$ and residues $r_j$, and let
  $\kappa'(i)=\kappa(i+1)$ be the shifted word.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item If $e_0>0$, then $(e_0-1,e_1-1,e_2-1,e_3-1)$ is a frame with
      residues $r_j-1$, and its start and finish vectors for $\kappa'$ equal
      those of $F$ for $\kappa$.
    \item If $e_0=0$, then $(e_1-1,e_2-1,e_3-1,n-1)$ is a frame with residues
      $\operatorname{rot}(r)_j-1$, and its start and finish vectors for
      $\kappa'$ are $\operatorname{rot}(\operatorname{start}^F_\kappa)$ and
      $\operatorname{rot}(\operatorname{finish}^F_\kappa)$.
  \end{enumerate}

def shiftOneOfZero (h0 : F.edge 0 = 0) : Frame n where
  edge := ![F.edge 1 - 1, F.edge 2 - 1, F.edge 3 - 1, n - 1]

    have h01 := F.strictMono (show (0 : Fin 4) < 1 by decide)
    have h12 := F.strictMono (show (1 : Fin 4) < 2 by decide)
    have h23 := F.strictMono (show (2 : Fin 4) < 3 by decide)

    · change F.edge 2 - 1 < n

deps.label: def:mt_slot_perm

blocks.tex:
(1) Monotonicity gives $e_j\ge e_0>0$, so subtracting $1$ is exact on the
  naturals, preserves strict order and keeps each edge below $n$.  The cast
  of $e_j-1$ is $r_j-1$, and $\kappa'(r_j-1)=\kappa(r_j)$,
  $\kappa'(r_j-1+1)=\kappa(r_j+1)$: the eight literal readings are unchanged.

  (2) From $0=e_0<e_1<e_2<e_3<n$ we get
  $e_1-1<e_2-1<e_3-1<n-1<n$, so the list is sorted and bounded.  The first
  three residues are $r_{j+1}-1$; the last is the cast of $n-1$, which is
  $-1=r_0-1$ since $r_0=0$.  So the residues are $\operatorname{rot}(r)-1$,
  and the shifted readings are $\kappa'(\operatorname{rot}(r)_j-1)=\kappa(\operatorname{rot}(r)_j)$,
  i.e.\ the rotated start vector, and likewise for finishes.  The edge that
  crossed the natural origin is the same actual edge, now listed last.

blocks.label: lem:mt_frame_reverse
blocks.title: reflection of a sorted frame
blocks.body:
For a frame $F$, the list $(n-1-e_3,\,n-1-e_2,\,n-1-e_1,\,n-1-e_0)$ is a
  frame, with residues $-1-\operatorname{rev}(r)_j$.  For the reflected word
  $\kappa^-(i)=\kappa(-i)$ its start vector is
  $\operatorname{rev}(\operatorname{finish}^F_\kappa)$ and its finish vector
  is $\operatorname{rev}(\operatorname{start}^F_\kappa)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.reverse_start
lean.code:
theorem reverse_start (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) :
    F.reverse.start (fun i => κ (-i)) = reverseFour (F.finish κ) := by
  funext j
  simp only [start, F.reverse_residue]
  fin_cases j <;> simp [reverseFour, finish, neg_sub]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.reverse_finish
lean.code:
theorem reverse_finish (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) :
    F.reverse.finish (fun i => κ (-i)) = reverseFour (F.start κ) := by
  funext j
  simp only [finish, F.reverse_residue]
  fin_cases j <;> simp [reverseFour, start]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.reverse_residue
lean.code:
theorem reverse_residue :
    F.reverse.residue = fun j => -1 - reverseFour F.residue j := by
  have hn : 1 ≤ n := by have := F.lt_n 0; omega
  have hj (j : Fin 4) : F.edge j ≤ n - 1 := by have := F.lt_n j; omega
  funext j
  fin_cases j <;>
    simp [residue, reverse, reverseFour, Nat.cast_sub (hj _),
      Nat.cast_sub hn]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.reverse
lean.code:
def reverse : Frame n where
  edge j := n - 1 - reverseFour F.edge j
  strictMono := by
    have h01 := F.strictMono (show (0 : Fin 4) < 1 by decide)
    have h12 := F.strictMono (show (1 : Fin 4) < 2 by decide)
    have h23 := F.strictMono (show (2 : Fin 4) < 3 by decide)
    have h3 := F.lt_n 3
    apply Fin.strictMono_iff_lt_succ.mpr
    intro j
    fin_cases j <;> simp [reverseFour] <;> omega
  lt_n := by
    intro j
    have hn : 0 < n := lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) (F.lt_n 0)
    exact lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) (by omega)

deps.label: def:mt_slot_perm

blocks.tex:
Since $e_j\le n-1$, the subtractions are exact; reversing a strictly
  increasing list and subtracting from $n-1$ gives a strictly increasing
  list, bounded by $n-1<n$.  The residue of the new slot $j$ is
  $(n-1)-r_{3-j}=-1-r_{3-j}$ in $\ZMod n$ (not $-r_{3-j}$: the reflection of
  the \emph{edge} from $r$ to $r+1$ is the edge from $-r-1$ to $-r$).  Hence
  the start reading of the new slot $j$ for $\kappa^-$ is
  $\kappa(-(-1-r_{3-j}))=\kappa(r_{3-j}+1)=t_{3-j}$ and its finish reading is
  $\kappa(-(-1-r_{3-j}+1))=\kappa(r_{3-j})=s_{3-j}$.

blocks.label: thm:mt_cyclic_anchor
blocks.title: cyclic transport of anchors
blocks.body:
Let $\kappa>0$.  A regular anchor of $\kappa$ gives a regular anchor of
  $i\mapsto\kappa(i+a)$ for every $a\in\ZMod n$, and conversely.  Thus
  $\kappa$ and each cyclic shift of $\kappa$ have regular anchors
  simultaneously.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.comp_add
lean.code:
noncomputable def comp_add (A : RegularFourAnchor κ) (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (a : ZMod n) : RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + a)) := by
  have hn : n ≠ 0 := by have := A.frame.lt_n 0; omega
  letI : NeZero n := ⟨hn⟩
  simpa only [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val] using A.comp_add_nat hκ a.val

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.nonempty_comp_add_iff
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_comp_add_iff (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (a : ZMod n) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + a))) ↔ Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨A⟩
    exact ⟨of_comp_add a hκ A⟩
  · rintro ⟨A⟩
    exact ⟨A.comp_add hκ a⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.comp_add_nat
lean.code:
noncomputable def comp_add_nat (A : RegularFourAnchor κ) (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (k : ℕ) : RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + (k : ZMod n))) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simpa using A
  | succ k ih =>
      have B := ih.comp_add_one (fun i => hκ _)
      simpa only [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, add_assoc, add_left_comm, add_comm] using B

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.comp_add_one
lean.code:
noncomputable def comp_add_one (A : RegularFourAnchor κ) (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) :
    RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + 1)) := by
  by_cases h0 : A.frame.edge 0 = 0
  · exact A.rotateReembed hκ (A.frame.shiftOneOfZero h0)
      (A.frame.shiftOneOfZero_start h0 κ) (A.frame.shiftOneOfZero_finish h0 κ)
  · have hp : 0 < A.frame.edge 0 := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h0
    exact A.reembed (A.frame.shiftOneOfPos hp)
      (A.frame.shiftOneOfPos_start hp κ) (A.frame.shiftOneOfPos_finish hp κ)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.of_comp_add
lean.code:
noncomputable def of_comp_add (a : ZMod n) (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (A : RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + a))) : RegularFourAnchor κ := by
  have B := A.comp_add (fun i => hκ _) (-a)
  simpa only [neg_add_cancel_right] using B

deps.label: thm:mt_reembed

blocks.tex:
\emph{One step.}  Let $(F,L)$ be an anchor of $\kappa$.  If $e_0>0$, the
  frame of \cref{lem:mt_frame_shift}(1) has the same literal readings for
  $i\mapsto\kappa(i+1)$, so \cref{lem:regular_four_reembed} gives an anchor
  with the same $L$.  If $e_0=0$, the frame of \cref{lem:mt_frame_shift}(2)
  has rotated endpoint vectors, and \cref{thm:mt_reembed}(1) gives the anchor
  with lengths $\operatorname{rot}L$; this uses positivity of $\kappa$.

  \emph{Iteration.}  By induction on $k\in\mathbb N$, applying the one-step
  transport to the already shifted (still positive) word gives an anchor of
  $i\mapsto\kappa(i+k)$.  For $a\in\ZMod n$ take $k=\operatorname{val}(a)$,
  whose cast is $a$ ($n\ne0$ because the frame has an edge below $n$).

  \emph{Inverse.}  An anchor of $i\mapsto\kappa(i+a)$ shifted by $-a$ is an
  anchor of $i\mapsto\kappa(i-a+a)=\kappa$.  The anchor witness, not only a
  realization, is carried in both directions.

blocks.label: thm:mt_reflected_anchor
blocks.title: reflected transport of anchors
blocks.body:
Let $\kappa>0$.  Then $\kappa$ has a regular anchor if and only if
  $i\mapsto\kappa(-i)$ has one.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.nonempty_comp_neg_iff
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_comp_neg_iff (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (-i))) ↔ Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨A⟩
    exact ⟨of_comp_neg hκ A⟩
  · rintro ⟨A⟩
    exact ⟨A.comp_neg hκ⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.comp_neg
lean.code:
noncomputable def comp_neg (A : RegularFourAnchor κ) (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) :
    RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (-i)) :=
  A.reverseReembed hκ A.frame.reverse (A.frame.reverse_start κ) (A.frame.reverse_finish κ)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.of_comp_neg
lean.code:
noncomputable def of_comp_neg (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (A : RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (-i))) : RegularFourAnchor κ := by
  have B := A.comp_neg (fun i => hκ _)
  simpa only [neg_neg] using B

blocks.tex:
Given an anchor $(F,L)$ of $\kappa$, the reversed frame of
  \cref{lem:mt_frame_reverse} has reversed and swapped endpoint vectors for
  $\kappa(-\,\cdot)$, so \cref{thm:mt_reembed}(2) gives the anchor
  $(F^{\mathrm{rev}},\operatorname{rev}L)$.  Conversely, reflect an anchor of
  $\kappa(-\,\cdot)$ once more (this word is positive too) and use
  $\kappa(-(-i))=\kappa(i)$.

blocks.label: def:mt_normalized
blocks.title: normalization at an index
blocks.body:
For $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ and $q\in\ZMod n$ put
  $\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,q)_i=\kappa_{i+q}/\kappa_q$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt
lean.code:
noncomputable def normalizedAt (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (q : ZMod n) (i : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  κ (i + q) / κ q
