lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.comp_neg
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.comp_neg {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H q : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q) :
    HighestSecondaryPeak (fun i => κ (-i)) (-H) (-q) := by
  refine ⟨fun h => hq.ne_global (neg_injective h), ?_, ?_⟩
  · constructor
    · simpa [neg_sub, add_comm] using hq.is_peak.2
    · simpa [neg_add, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hq.is_peak.1
  · intro i hi hpeak
    have hi' : -i ≠ H := by intro e; apply hi; simpa using congrArg Neg.neg e
    have hpeak' : IsStrictLocalMax κ (-i) := by
      constructor
      · simpa [neg_add, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hpeak.2
      · simpa [neg_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hpeak.1
    simpa using hq.maximal (-i) hi' hpeak'

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.div_pos
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.div_pos {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H q : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    HighestSecondaryPeak (fun i => κ i / s) H q := by
  refine ⟨hq.ne_global, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨div_lt_div_of_pos_right hq.is_peak.1 hs,
      div_lt_div_of_pos_right hq.is_peak.2 hs⟩
  · intro i hi hpeak
    have hpeak' : IsStrictLocalMax κ i :=
      ⟨(div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right hs).mp hpeak.1,
        (div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right hs).mp hpeak.2⟩
    exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (hq.maximal i hi hpeak') hs.le

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.comp_add
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.comp_add {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H q : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q) (a : ZMod n) :
    HighestSecondaryPeak (fun i => κ (i + a)) (H - a) (q - a) := by
  refine ⟨fun h => hq.ne_global (by simpa using congrArg (fun x => x + a) h), ?_, ?_⟩
  · constructor
    · simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using hq.is_peak.1
    · simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using hq.is_peak.2
  · intro i hi hpeak
    have hi' : i + a ≠ H := by intro e; apply hi; exact eq_sub_iff_add_eq.mpr e
    have hpeak' : IsStrictLocalMax κ (i + a) := by
      constructor
      · simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using hpeak.1
      · simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using hpeak.2
    simpa using hq.maximal (i + a) hi' hpeak'

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt_pos
lean.code:
theorem normalizedAt_pos {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (q : ZMod n) :
    ∀ i, 0 < normalizedAt κ q i := fun i => div_pos (hκ (i + q)) (hκ q)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.adjacent_ne_comp_neg
lean.code:
theorem adjacent_ne_comp_neg {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) :
    ∀ i, κ (-i) ≠ κ (-(i + 1)) := by
  intro i
  simpa [neg_add, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm, add_left_comm, add_assoc]
    using (hne (-i - 1)).symm

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.normalizedAt
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.normalizedAt {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H q : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q) (hpos : 0 < κ q) :
    HighestSecondaryPeak (normalizedAt κ q) (H - q) 0 := by
  change HighestSecondaryPeak (fun i => κ (i + q) / κ q) (H - q) 0
  simpa only [sub_self] using (hq.comp_add q).div_pos hpos

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt_adjacent_ne
lean.code:
theorem normalizedAt_adjacent_ne {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) {q : ZMod n} (hpos : 0 < κ q) :
    ∀ i, normalizedAt κ q i ≠ normalizedAt κ q (i + 1) := by
  intro i hh
  have heq := (div_left_inj' hpos.ne').mp hh
  apply hne (i + q)
  simpa [add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using heq

blocks.tex:
(1),(2) The maps $i\mapsto i+a$ and $i\mapsto-i$ are bijections of
  $\ZMod n$ which carry neighbours to neighbours; reflection exchanges the
  two neighbours $i\pm1$, so the two defining inequalities of a strict local
  maximum are exchanged.  Hence strict local maxima, their values, the
  condition $i\ne H$ and maximality among them correspond exactly.
  (3) Division by $s>0$ preserves and reflects all strict and nonstrict
  comparisons.  (4) combines (1) with $a=q$ and (3) with $s=\kappa_q$; then
  $\mu_0=\kappa_q/\kappa_q=1$.  Positivity of $\mu$ is a quotient of
  positives.  Adjacent inequality of $\mu$ at $i$ is that of $\kappa$ at
  $i+q$ after cancelling $\kappa_q\ne0$; for the reflected word, the pair
  $\kappa_{-i},\kappa_{-(i+1)}$ is the adjacent pair of $\kappa$ at $-i-1$.

When the capstone needs it, strict global maximality transfers in the same
way: if $\kappa_i<\kappa_H$ for $i
e H$, then $\mu_i<\mu_{H-q}$ for
$i
e H-q$, since $i+q
e H$ and division by $\kappa_q>0$ is monotone.

blocks.label: thm:mt_restore_normalization
blocks.title: restoring scale and origin
blocks.body:
Let $\kappa>0$ and $q\in\ZMod n$.  If $\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,q)$
  has a regular anchor, so does $\kappa$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_normalizedAt
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_normalizedAt
    {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {q : ZMod n}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (hA : Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor (normalizedAt κ q))) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  obtain ⟨A⟩ := hA
  have B := A.scale (hκ q)
  have B' : RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + q)) := by
    convert B using 1
    funext i
    dsimp only [Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt]
    field_simp [(hκ q).ne']
  exact ⟨RegularFourAnchor.of_comp_add q hκ B'⟩

blocks.tex:
Scale the anchor by $s=\kappa_q>0$ (\cref{lem:mt_anchor_scale}): this gives
  an anchor of $i\mapsto\kappa_q\cdot\kappa_{i+q}/\kappa_q=\kappa_{i+q}$.  Then
  undo the shift by $q$ (\cref{thm:mt_cyclic_anchor}, which applies because
  $\kappa>0$).  The anchor is transported before any opening; realizability
  is never used as an intermediate.

blocks.label: thm:mt_forward_terminal
blocks.title: the forward terminal branch
blocks.body:
Let $\mu>0$ be adjacent-unequal, $0$ a highest secondary peak for $H$,
  $\mu_0=1<\mu_H$, and
  $\Phi(\mu_1,\mu_{H-1},\mu_H,\mu_{-1})\ge0$ (equality included).  Then $\mu$
  has a regular anchor.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_forward_terminal
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_forward_terminal
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H 0)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hzero : κ 0 = 1) (hH : 1 < κ H)
    (hflag : 0 ≤ firstPairFlag (κ 1) (κ (H - 1)) (κ H) (κ (-1))) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  apply hq.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_rising_terminal hκ hne hzero hH
  simpa only [natPred_val_residue hq.ne_global.symm] using hflag

blocks.tex:
By \cref{lem:mt_normalized_entry}, $H\ne0$ and the flag equals the flag
  with the natural predecessor $\operatorname{val}(H)-1$, which is the
  hypothesis of \cref{thm:nfp_rising_anchor}(3).  That theorem uses the
  mountain and the normalized low entry to invoke the least-transition
  selector \cref{lem:nfp_rising_transition} on the rising leg $[a,h]$; the
  selected index $i$ satisfies $a\le i<h$ with the genuine predecessor and
  successor inequalities (including the case $i=a$, where the predecessor
  comparison is with the low entry), and the first-transition producer on
  the frame $0,i-1,i,n-1$ (\cref{lem:nfp_frame}) gives the anchor.

blocks.label: thm:mt_backward_terminal
blocks.title: the backward terminal branch
blocks.body:
Let $\mu>0$ be adjacent-unequal, $0$ a highest secondary peak for $H$,
  $\mu_0=1<\mu_H$, and $\Phi(\mu_{-1},\mu_{H+1},\mu_H,\mu_1)\ge0$.  Then $\mu$
  has a regular anchor.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_backward_terminal
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_backward_terminal
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H 0)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hzero : κ 0 = 1) (hH : 1 < κ H)
    (hflag : 0 ≤ firstPairFlag (κ (-1)) (κ (H + 1)) (κ H) (κ 1)) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  have hq' : HighestSecondaryPeak (fun i => κ (-i)) (-H) 0 := by
    simpa using hq.comp_neg
  apply (RegularFourAnchor.nonempty_comp_neg_iff hκ).mp
  apply hq'.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_forward_terminal (fun i => hκ (-i))
    (adjacent_ne_comp_neg hne) (by simpa using hzero) (by simpa using hH)
  simpa [neg_sub, add_comm] using hflag

blocks.tex:
Let $\mu^-(i)=\mu(-i)$.  By \cref{lem:mt_peak_symmetry}(2), $0=-0$ is a
  highest secondary peak for $-H$ in $\mu^-$; $\mu^-$ is positive and
  adjacent-unequal, $\mu^-_0=1<\mu_H=\mu^-_{-H}$.  Its forward terminal flag
  is
  \[
    \Phi\bigl(\mu^-_1,\mu^-_{-H-1},\mu^-_{-H},\mu^-_{-1}\bigr)
      =\Phi\bigl(\mu_{-1},\mu_{H+1},\mu_H,\mu_1\bigr),
  \]
  exactly the backward flag of $\mu$: reflection exchanges $p=\mu_1$ and
  $l=\mu_{-1}$ and sends the predecessor $-H-1$ of $-H$ to the successor
  $H+1$ of $H$.  There is no sign change of the flag.  So
  \cref{thm:mt_forward_terminal} gives an anchor of $\mu^-$, and
  \cref{thm:mt_reflected_anchor} restores the orientation, with its derivative
  witness.
